name: BQ27441DRZR-G1B
title: Single-cell Li-ion system-side fuel gauge with I2C interface (bq27441-G1)
summary: The bq27441-G1 is a battery fuel gauge for one Li-ion cell that sits on the system board, not in the pack, and is powered straight from the cell through its own 1.8 V LDO. It measures cell voltage, current through a 10 mΩ high-side sense resistor and temperature, and runs the Impedance Track algorithm to report remaining capacity in mAh, state of charge in percent and state of health over a 400 kHz I2C bus. The G1A and G1B versions carry different preloaded LiCoO2 chemistry profiles for 4.2 V and 4.3 to 4.35 V charge limits.
key_figures: 93 µA NORMAL, 21 µA SLEEP, 9 µA HIBERNATE, 0.6 µA SHUTDOWN (typ)

notes: CHEM_ID, DM_CODE and firmware version can be read back from the device with the CHEM_ID, DM_CODE and FW_VERSION control subcommands.

The orderable list also carries BQ27441DRZR-G1AG4 and the .A variants (BQ27441DRZR-G1A.A, BQ27441DRZR-G1AG4.A, BQ27441DRZR-G1B.A, BQ27441DRZT-G1A.A, BQ27441DRZT-G1B.A), with the same package, packing and marking as their base numbers.
All are RoHS: yes, NiPdAu lead finish, MSL level 2 at 260 °C peak for 1 year, rated –40 °C to 85 °C.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C data, slave to the host. Needs an external pullup, 10 kΩ typical. If the pullups can be switched off during operation, add 1 MΩ to VSS so the input does not float.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C clock, slave to the host. Needs an external pullup, 10 kΩ typical. If the pullups can be switched off during operation, add 1 MΩ to VSS so the input does not float.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Ground. This pin is the device's ground reference.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Not connected inside; leave open or connect to VSS.

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Output of the internal 1.8 V regulator. Bypass to VSS with a 0.47 µF ceramic capacitor. Not meant to supply other circuits.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Supplies the LDO and is the cell-voltage measurement input. Run a Kelvin sense line to the pack positive terminal (PACKP) and fit a 1 µF capacitor from BAT to VSS near the IC.

pins.name: SRN
pins.function: Coulomb-counter input, system side. Kelvin-connect to the end of the 10 mΩ high-side sense resistor that goes to VSYS.

pins.name: SRP
pins.function: Coulomb-counter input, battery side. Kelvin-connect to the end of the 10 mΩ sense resistor at PACKP. The gauge comes calibrated for a 10 mΩ, 1 % resistor, so no calibration is needed.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Not connected inside; leave open or connect to VSS.

pins.name: BIN
pins.function: Battery-present input. With OpConfig [BI_PU_EN] = 1 (the default) a low level means a battery is inserted. For a removable pack the pack pulls BIN low through its resistor, typically its 10 kΩ thermistor, and the board pulls it up with 1.8 MΩ to VDD so it reads high with the pack out. For an embedded cell keep [BI_PU_EN] = 1 and fit 10 kΩ from BIN to VSS. With [BI_PU_EN] = 0 the host reports insertion and removal with BAT_INSERT and BAT_REMOVE. Keep a 10 kΩ pulldown to VSS even when the pin is unused. Never short BIN straight to a rail; a pullup may go to VDD only, never to another supply.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Not connected inside; leave open or connect to VSS.

pins.name: GPOUT
pins.function: Interrupt output. By default ([BATLOWEN] cleared) it gives interrupt pulses (SOC_INT), for instance when state of charge changes; with OpConfig [BATLOWEN] set it signals BAT_LOW instead. [GPIOPOL] sets its polarity. Do not leave it floating: a 10 kΩ pullup is suggested. A toggle on GPOUT brings the gauge out of SHUTDOWN, so wiring it to a host GPIO is advised.

pins.name: PWPD
pins.function: Exposed pad under the package; solder it to the board. Connected to PGND in the typical application.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The gauge watches a one-cell pack on a three-way connector (PACKP, BIN, PACKN). BAT is tied to PACKP with C2 (1.0 µF) to ground beside it; C1 (0.47 µF) bypasses the 1.8 V VDD output. R1, 0.010 Ω at 1 %, is in the positive lead between PACKP and the system load or charger (VSYS); SRP senses its pack end and SRN its system end. SDA, SCL and GPOUT each have a 5.1 kΩ pullup to VPU. BIN is pulled up to VPU by R5 (1.8 MΩ) and runs to pin 2 of J5. NC pins are left open and VSS and the exposed pad go to PGND.

operation.text: Current is found from the voltage across a small sense resistor in the battery path, and is integrated by a coulomb counter. With a cell attached the gauge works out cell impedance from current, open-circuit voltage and loaded voltage, and the Impedance Track algorithm uses these to predict state of charge, adjusting for ageing, self-discharge, temperature and load rate. Cell temperature comes from an on-chip sensor or can be written by the host. Fuller detail is in the technical reference manual SLUUAC9.

Settings live in one-time-programmable NVM. From the factory, the chemistry-related parameters are loaded and most others are zero. On reset the OTP contents are copied into RAM data memory, and every RAM parameter must be set up before use: written into data memory during development, or programmed into OTP for production. Default and typical values are in chapter 6 of SLUUAC9.

The gauge moves between INITIALIZATION, NORMAL, SLEEP and HIBERNATE on its own as conditions change, and the host can force some of these. SHUTDOWN is entered on command: SHUTDOWN_ENABLE then SHUTDOWN; the LDO turns off within 250 ms (tSHDN) and the supply current drops to 0.6 µA typical. To wake it, hold GPOUT low for at least 10 µs and then raise it; VDD returns about 8 ms after the rising edge and the gauge talks again after tPUCD.

The LDO starts when VBAT rises past 2 V (UVLOIT+) and shuts off automatically when VBAT falls below 1.95 V (UVLOIT–). At first power the VDD output appears after about 13 ms, and the gauge is ready on I2C about 250 ms after the supply rises, firmware start included.

The bus engine handles single and incremental reads, quick reads, and single-byte or incremental writes. The 7-bit address is fixed at 1010101, so the address byte is 0xAA for a write and 0xAB for a read. An internal address pointer steps on each acknowledged byte, so quick reads and writes reach consecutive command locations. Standard commands are 2-byte words; extended commands range from one byte to many. Writing a read-only location gets a NACK after the data, and reading above 0x6B gets a NACK on the command.

If the bus stays low for 2 s the gauge lets go of SDA and SCL; if something outside is holding a line low it then drops into SLEEP. The gauge may stretch the clock in any mode: up to 100 µs in SLEEP and HIBERNATE while it wakes for a packet, and up to 4 ms in INITIALIZATION and NORMAL.

Leave at least 66 µs of bus-free time, t(BUF), between packets sent to the gauge. Above 100 kHz send each byte as its own 1-byte write; at 100 kHz or less a 2-byte incremental write of a subcommand is acceptable. A read-write standard command needs at least 2 s before its result is updated. Read-only standard commands need no wait, but no standard command may be sent over twice per second, or the watchdog may expire and reset the gauge.

BAT both powers the gauge and measures the cell. A ceramic capacitor at BAT keeps load ripple off this high-impedance node and so out of the voltage reading; it matters most with pulsed loads such as phones and is advised in every design. Fit at least 1 µF from BAT to VSS, and it is required when the lead from the pack can pick up noise. VDD, about 1.8 V, needs at least 0.47 µF to VSS. Both capacitors go close to the IC on short traces.

Any error in the resistance between SRP and SRN becomes current error, so the resistor should have tight tolerance and low TCR. The usual pick is 1 % tolerance, 50 ppm drift and 1 W rating, at 10 mΩ, which the gauge is calibrated for.

Kelvin-connect SRP and SRN right at the sense resistor pads, SRP on the pack side and SRN on the system side, and Kelvin-connect BAT at the pack positive terminal with short leads. Pin 3 (VSS) is the device ground; the capacitor ground goes to power ground through a via. Use copper pours for the battery power path to cut IR loss. The I2C pullups go to the host's pullup supply, not to the gauge's VDD; if they are switched off in low-power operation, add 1 MΩ pulldowns to VSS on SCL and SDA. Choose pullup values for the pullup voltage and bus capacitance. An unused GPOUT is still pulled up to VDD with 4.7 kΩ or 10 kΩ. Without a pack thermistor on BIN, pull BIN to VSS with 10 kΩ; never short it to VDD or VSS.

The DRZ package is a 12-pin VSON, 1 mm maximum height, with an exposed thermal pad (pin 13) that must be soldered to the board for heat and mechanical strength. Vias in the pad are optional; vias under paste are best filled, plugged or tented. The suggested stencil prints 79 % of the exposed pad area with a 0.1 mm stencil.
